prompt.context: Your client is CNB Movies, a national movie theater company with $2 billion in annual revenue. In recent years, movie theaters have seen record high demand for Marvel and DC Comics movies, and CNB is considering ways to capitalize on this demand. One option is to offer 24-hour opening weekend screenings for these movies.
prompt.question: The company has hired you to advise on the decision. Should they offer this experience?

clarifying_info.q: When does CNB want to implement this?
What counts as an opening weekend?
clarifying_info.a: Opening weekend starts Thursday night and ends Sunday at 11:59 PM — 3 nights.

clarifying_info.q: Is this a full rollout or a test?
clarifying_info.a: CNB wants to test one theater first. If successful, the company would roll out to all 400 theaters in the US.
$15 for adults, $10 for children and seniors.
None of CNB's competitors currently offer this experience.

clarifying_info.q: Does CNB have the capital to fund this?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, CNB Movies is capable of financing this on its own.

exhibits.title: Expected Seat Utilization Per Showing
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing seat utilization percentages broken down by audience segment (Children, Adults, Seniors) for three overnight showtimes: 12:00 AM, 3:00 AM, and 6:00 AM. Each theater has 300 seats.

exhibits.title: Daily Cost Structure Per Theater (Current Costs)
exhibits.shows: A table listing the current daily cost components per theater for staff, concessions, concession maintenance, and projector maintenance.

framework: Revenue: ticket sales (adults at $15, children/seniors at $10) and concession sales
Costs: staff (cashiers, ticket collectors, film operators, cleaning, security), concession COGS, concession maintenance, projector maintenance, utilities
Financial risks: can the projector operate 24 hours without additional capital maintenance costs?
Competitive considerations: no competitor currently offers this; potential first-mover advantage
Pricing opportunity: potential to charge a premium for late-night novelty
Demand variability: concession purchase rates may differ at unusual showtimes
Opportunity cost: alternative uses of capital or operational capacity

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate total ticket revenue per night across all three showtimes.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the mixed-price formula for each showtime using the segment percentages and 300 seats, then sum across the three times.

math.setup: Ticket Rev per showtime = 300 seats * [(% children * $10) + (% adults * $15) + (% seniors * $10)]

questions.prompt: Calculate concession revenue per night, given average concession spend of $10 per person.
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply $10 by total attendees at each showtime (300 * utilization rate), then sum.

math.setup: Concession Rev per showtime = $10 * (300 * total utilization %)

questions.prompt: Calculate total revenue over the full 3-night opening weekend.
questions.guidance: Sum ticket and concession revenue per night, then multiply by 3 nights.

math.setup: Total weekend revenue = (ticket rev + concession rev) per night * 3

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2 and the cost increase assumptions, calculate total costs over the 3-night opening weekend.
questions.guidance: Apply each cost increase percentage to the current daily cost, then multiply by 3 nights. Cost increases provided by interviewer: Staff +50%, Concessions +50%, Concession Maintenance +25%, Projector Maintenance +10%.

math.setup: New daily cost per line item = Current cost * (1 + increase %); Total weekend cost = Sum of new daily costs * 3

questions.prompt: Calculate incremental profit from the 24-hour model for one theater over an opening weekend, and the profit margin.
questions.guidance: Subtract total weekend costs from total weekend revenue. Divide profit by revenue for margin.

math.setup: Incremental profit = Total revenue - Total costs; Margin = Profit / Revenue

brainstorming.prompt: What are some additional factors that our client should consider before making their final decision?

categories.name: Demand & Customer
ideas: Risk of cannibalizing existing (daytime/evening) customer base
Customer and demographic analysis by region — demand may vary
Sensitivity of demand assumptions; attendance projections may be optimistic

categories.name: Financial & Operational
ideas: Upfront and ongoing marketing costs not captured in the model
Long-term capital expenditure from running projectors 24 hours (wear and tear)
Sensitivity analysis on both revenue and cost assumptions

categories.name: Competitive & Strategic
ideas: How will competitors react — could they quickly copy this model?
If CNB does not act, could they lose customers to a competitor that does?
First-mover advantage and potential to build brand loyalty

categories.name: Rollout & Execution
ideas: Whether to roll out to all 400 theaters or a subset based on market criteria
Which movies to select — not all blockbusters have same demand profile
Which geographic markets to prioritize for rollout

categories.name: Marketing & Brand
ideas: Word-of-mouth and PR value of offering a novel experience
Long-term market share gains from being the only chain to offer this
Develop criteria for selecting films eligible for the 24-hour format

recommendation: CNB Movies should implement the 24-hour opening weekend experience. The model generates $10,800 in incremental profit per theater per opening weekend, representing a ~22% profit margin.
Offering this experience also creates a competitive advantage for high-grossing Marvel and DC movies, as no competitor currently offers it.
risks: Demand and cost assumptions may need further validation before a national rollout
Projections are likely to vary by theater and geography
A film could underperform ('be a flop'), making the incremental costs hard to recoup
Running projectors continuously may accelerate capital maintenance costs beyond the 10% assumption
next_steps: Develop a marketing strategy to drive awareness and demand for the 24-hour experience
Conduct sensitivity analysis on key demand and cost assumptions
Design an optimal rollout strategy across US theaters and define selection criteria for which movies and which markets qualify for this model
